methodology: Each DEM was parsed once into identical sources for format comparisons. Saves were repeated three times per format.
Both formats use the current common reader. This is a format comparison, not a measurement of the original 9318ed9 double-decoding worker.

Open/seek/switch/release come from 24 fresh GUI processes. Final portable measurements use the one-shot-verifier build and separate samples; older portable Main allocation experiments are not included in the final memory peaks.
New-process open means a fresh process with OS file cache retained. It does not mean a cold physical disk.
GUI IPC times are measured inside Renderer around the real API; CDP transfer and post-request JSON/SHA verification are excluded.
Main and Utility memory comes from passive 100ms observers on exact copies of built code; Renderer heap uses CDP, working sets use app.getAppMetrics.
JS heap, RSS/working set, external and ArrayBuffer values are separate. ArrayBuffers are included in external; no complete native allocator profile is claimed.
Blocking work can hide brief sampled heap peaks. Lifetime maxRSS and process working-set high water supplement sampled observations.
Tool shared parse/report includes independent source identity checks; it is not a GUI import SLA or three independent DEM parse timings.
Raw archives, logs, screenshots and timelines stay in owned temporary directories; only this compact evidence is committed.

memory.interpretation: Named phases only. Node peaks are single-process role high waters; Utility working set sums simultaneous Analysis and Verification processes. Tracked total is measured at a common timestamp, not a sum of independent role maxima. Working sets include shared pages and are not PSS or complete application physical memory (GPU/network excluded). null means unobserved, not zero.

limits: Development built app with the existing Main DEM-dialog seam; no packaged native-dialog automation.
Original DEMs remain in place. Offline opens have no DEM path injection and use library.open; no claim of OS-level access denial.

Cancellation, wrong DEM, I/O/transaction faults and process interruption use the focused Main/library regression suites; this four-parse script exercises successful native reanalysis and offline restoration.

nativeReanalysis.interpretation: Node RSS and JS heap are different measurements. Utility totals include AnalysisUtility and VerificationUtility; their separate columns expose transferred verification work. Node peaks are per-process role high waters; working-set values sum simultaneous processes within each role, including overlapping old/new Utilities during a switch. external includes native-bound objects; arrayBuffers is a subset and must not be added to it. Chromium backingStorage/embedder values are CDP observations, not a complete native heap. Working sets come from app.getAppMetrics; Node lifetime maxRSS catches RSS spikes between timers. No GC is requested. Brief JS heap spikes during blocking work can fall between samples. A phase with no observations returns null; an observed working-set sample with no active library Utility is measured zero. Lifecycle creationTime is the OS timestamp, first/last/absence are 100ms observations, and nodeObserverExitAt is present only when the normal Node exit observer ran. Whole-flow peaks include the alternate match; use the named phases and matchId for per-match open/seek/release comparisons.
